name: Aalborg East Full-Scale EBPR Activated Sludge Community
description: An engineered full-scale activated sludge microbial community from the Aalborg East wastewater treatment plant in Denmark carrying out enhanced biological phosphorus removal. The community was profiled with an 18.2 Gb Illumina metagenome and qFISH, revealing phosphate-removal organisms including Candidatus Accumulibacter and Tetrasphaera-related Actinobacteria, flanking substrate-providing bacteria, and metagenomic enrichment for phosphate metabolism and biofilm/floc formation functions.

name: Acetobacterium woodii-Clostridium drakei CO2 Electrolysis Coculture
description: A defined anaerobic synthetic coculture that combines a lactate-producing Acetobacterium woodii mutant with Clostridium drakei to convert CO2 and H2 into longer-chain products. A. woodii fixes CO2 with H2 and is engineered to release lactate, which C. drakei uses as an intermediate for chain elongation to caproic acid. The system is DOE-relevant because it couples microbial CO2 valorization with in situ water electrolysis or CO2/H2 gas feeding for production of value chemicals.

name: Acetylene-Fueled Trichloroethene Dechlorination Groundwater Enrichment
description: A microbial community enriched from TCE/PCE-contaminated groundwater and amended with acetylene (C2H2) as the sole electron donor and organic carbon source. The stable enrichment performs reductive dechlorination of trichloroethene (TCE) and tetrachloroethene (PCE), coupling acetylenotrophy to organohalide respiration. Metagenomic analysis of the stable community identified a novel anaerobic acetylenotroph in the phylum Actinobacteria, expanding the known diversity of this metabolism beyond previously documented Pelobacter SFB93 + Dehalococcoides mccartyi laboratory cocultures.

name: Achromobacter-Enterobacter SL8-SL12 Cadmium Immobilization Coculture
description: A defined two-member bacterial coculture assembled from the Cd-contaminated mine-area soil isolates Achromobacter sp. SL8 and Enterobacter sp. SL12 to immobilize cadmium. In 100 mg/L Cd2+ LB assays the SL8-SL12 coculture removed 80.9% of dissolved Cd after 7 days, exceeding both monocultures at the same Cd dose; Cd partitioning, microscopy, and spectroscopy associated this performance with CdS bioprecipitation, intracellular Cd accumulation, surface aggregation with possible EPS involvement, and phosphate-, amino-, and hydroxyl-bearing surface groups. In greenhouse Chinese-cabbage pots the inoculated coculture decreased bioavailable soil Cd fractions and lowered Cd in aboveground cabbage tissue under high Cd stress.

name: Acidic Nitrification Minimal Consortium
description: A minimal aerobic ammonia-oxidizing consortium from three acidic nitrification bioreactors operated between pH 2.0 and 5.0. Genome-resolved meta-omics and chemical measurements linked the pH 5.0 cultures to a novel Nitrosococcaceae ammonia-oxidizing bacterium, "Candidatus Nitrosoglobus kelleri", that reached up to 56% relative abundance and linked the strongly simplified pH 2.0 community to "Ca. Nitrosoglobus kelleri" together with Mycobacterium species.

name: Aerobic Denitrification Disturbance-Stable SynCom
description: A three-member aerobic denitrification SMC that maintains function under dibutyl phthalate and levofloxacin disturbances through division of labor.

name: Aerobic Denitrification Quorum-Quenching SynCom
description: A three-member aerobic denitrification SynCom whose quorum-quenching and AHL-mediated interactions improve nitrate removal.

name: Alaska Tundra Permafrost Iron-Redox Community
description: A northern Alaska wet sedge tundra microbial community studied across the permafrost thaw gradient, where iron-cycling Gammaproteobacteria - the heterotrophic Fe(III)-reducing Rhodoferax sp. and the chemoautotrophic Fe(II)-oxidizing Gallionella sp. - become numerically dominant during extended anaerobic thaw of transition-zone and permafrost soils. Functional gene abundance shows that Fe(III) reduction and Fe(II) oxidation increase in lockstep with benzoate degradation and pyruvate metabolism, supporting a carbon-cycling model in which acetate and benzoate are oxidized to CO2 coupled to Fe(III) reduction. Concurrent decreases in CH4-metabolism gene abundance suggest that dissimilatory Fe(III) reduction competitively suppresses acetoclastic methanogenesis under the reducing thaw conditions examined.

name: Alfalfa Stress-Adapted Bacterial SynCom
description: A defined five-member bacterial SynCom assembled from plant-associated Bacillus sp. G3, Bacillus sp. G12, Acinetobacter sp. G13, Plantibacter flavus M251, and Plantibacter flavus M259 isolates from stress-affected Canadian environments. Shipar et al. validated the members for in-vitro plant growth-promoting and abiotic-stress traits, mixed equal volumes of OD600-standardized LB cultures, and applied the mixture twice to alfalfa grown in non-sterilized field soil under well-watered, moderate-drought, and severe-drought growth-chamber regimes.

name: Algal-Methanotroph Biogas Valorization Coculture
description: A laboratory enriched haloalkaliphilic microalga-methanotroph co-culture assembled by mixing a halotolerant methanotrophic consortium with a non-axenic algal culture. Triplicate 2.1 L gas-tight glass bioreactors containing 450 mL 6% NaCl mineral salt medium were supplied with a 70:30 CH4:CO2 biogas headspace under light; after two external O2 additions, the culture maintained methane oxidation via algal O2 production and removed 92% CH4 and 89% CO2 while producing ectoine, hydroxyectoine, and carotenoids. Shotgun metagenomics identified Chlorella vulgaris and Dunaliella viridis as the dominant Chlorophyta, Methylotuvimicrobium as the dominant methanotroph, and Methylophaga plus Methylonatrum as co-dominant methylotrophs.

name: Altered Schaedler Flora Gnotobiotic Mouse Community
description: The altered Schaedler flora (ASF) is an eight-member defined murine gut bacterial community used in gnotobiotic mice. The community was developed as a standardized, culturable intestinal flora from mouse-derived bacteria and has been used for decades to study host-microbiota relationships, member stability, spatial distribution, immune effects, and genome-informed community metabolism.

name: AM-AB Chlorella-MLSS Wastewater Consortium
description: A microalga-bacteria wastewater-treatment consortium assembled by combining activated Chlorella vulgaris with separately activated mixed liquor suspended solids (MLSS) bacteria in an outdoor high-rate algal pond. Kumar et al. 2026 called this pairing an activated microalgae-activated bacteria, or AM-AB, consortium and reported rapid nitrogen, phosphate, and biological oxygen demand removal during biological wastewater treatment.

name: AMD Acidophile Heterotroph Network
description: A heterotrophic microbial network in acid mine drainage (AMD) systems dominated by Acidiphilium species and related acidophilic heterotrophs. This community plays a crucial role in coupling carbon and iron cycles in extremely acidic environments, supporting autotrophic iron oxidizers through organic matter processing and nutrient remineralization. The network thrives at pH 2-4 in AMD sites globally, where heterotrophs metabolize organic compounds produced by autotrophs or released from lysed cells, preventing organic carbon accumulation that would inhibit autotrophic iron oxidizers. Key members include Acidiphilium multivorum (facultative Fe(III) reducer and organic carbon degrader), Ferrimicrobium acidiphilum (iron-oxidizing heterotroph and dissolved organic carbon remover), Acidocella facilis (obligate aerobic heterotroph), Acidisphaera rubrifaciens (photoheterotrophic bacteriochlorophyll producer), and Acidobacterium capsulatum (chemoorganotrophic acidophile). These organisms collectively perform organic matter degradation, ferric iron reduction, biofilm formation, and nutrient cycling. The heterotroph-autotroph coupling maintains community stability by removing inhibitory organic carbon, recycling nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus), generating ferrous iron for autotrophic energy generation, and facilitating metal tolerance through extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) production. This network represents a critical functional guild in AMD ecosystems, enabling the persistence of autotrophic iron-oxidizing communities through metabolic cooperation and resource partitioning.

name: AMD Nitrososphaerota Archaeal Community
description: A novel archaeal community from acid mine drainage environments dominated by ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) of the phylum Nitrososphaerota (formerly Thaumarchaeota). This community represents a unique nitrogen-cycling system operating at extremely low pH (2.5-4.5) where archaeal nitrifiers outcompete bacterial ammonia oxidizers. The dominant members include acidophilic AOA such as Candidatus Nitrosotalea devanaterra and Nitrososphaera-like archaea that possess extraordinary substrate affinity (Km 0.6-2.8 nM for NH3) and specialized adaptations for acidophily. These archaea oxidize ammonia to nitrite through the copper-containing ammonia monooxygenase (AMO) enzyme while maintaining cytoplasmic pH homeostasis in extremely acidic environments. The community also includes supporting acidophilic archaea from Thermoplasmata (Ferroplasma, Acidiplasma) that provide ecosystem services including organic matter processing and metal tolerance. Unique features include: (1) Amt-type ammonium transporters enabling NH4+ uptake rather than NH3 diffusion, (2) urea hydrolysis pathways providing localized ammonia generation, (3) extensive cell surface glycosylation reducing proton permeability, and (4) metabolic cooperation with nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (Nitrospira, Leptospirillum) completing the nitrification pathway. This system demonstrates how archaeal nitrifiers dominate nitrogen cycling in acidic environments where bacterial counterparts cannot function, with AOA abundance 3-10 fold higher than AOB in AMD sediments. The community thrives in acid sulfate soils, acid mine drainage sediments, and acidic tailings, representing a critical component of nitrogen cycling in the 30% of Earth's soils with pH <5.5. Based on genomic data from NCBI BioProject PRJNA1261802 and related AMD archaeal community studies.

name: Amsterdam 10-Species Gut Invasion SynCom
description: A defined ten-strain human gut bacterial synthetic-community panel used to quantify soluble, environmentally mediated interactions and predict community assembly and invasion outcomes. van Leeuwen et al. generated cell-free YCFA spent media from each DSMZ strain, grew every other strain in 40% spent plus 60% fresh YCFA medium, validated generalized Lotka-Volterra predictions with two- to four-member YCFA co-cultures, and tested whether Escherichia coli DSM 18039 or Bacteroides ovatus DSM 1896 could invade predicted stable resident assemblages.

name: Anabaena / MGS-1 Anaerobic-Digestion Methanogen Consortium
description: An anaerobic-digestion microbial consortium studied as part of a bioregenerative life-support concept for Mars: cyanobacterial biomass (Anabaena sp.), which can be grown on Martian resources, is anaerobically digested to mobilize nutrients (ammonium and phosphate) for use as a crop fertilizer, with biogas as a co-product. Ramalho et al. (2025, Bioresource Technology) tested three microbial communities for their ability to digest Anabaena biomass in three matrices — a minimal medium, 200 g/L MGS-1 Mars regolith simulant, and water. In minimal medium the taxonomic (16S) analysis revealed a SYNTROPHIC community: fermentative bacteria degrade the cyanobacterial biomass and cross-feed hydrogenotrophic methanogenic archaea (interspecies H2/CO2 transfer driving methanogenesis). In the MGS-1 regolith matrix, however, the methanogens were outcompeted by sulfate-reducing bacteria, and the regolith also adsorbed organics and lowered phosphate/ammonium recovery. The Anabaena biomass here is the digestion FEEDSTOCK (substrate) rather than a live member of the digesting consortium. All communities produced ammonium and removed organic carbon, supporting the viability of a Mars-relevant bioprocess for fertilizer production. The specific dominant genera resolved by the paper's 16S analysis are reported in the full text, which is paywalled; only the functional guilds (fermentative bacteria, hydrogenotrophic methanogens, sulfate-reducing bacteria) are named in the openly available abstract and are therefore represented here as interactions/roles rather than as NCBITaxon-grounded members.

name: Anaerobic Indole-Degrading Sludge Consortium
description: A long-term acclimated anaerobic sludge consortium established to transform the nitrogen heterocycle indole under laboratory conditions. Meng et al. (2026) combined anaerobic degradation assays, metabolite profiling, metatranscriptomics, and genome-resolved metagenomics after 120 days of acclimation; the enrichment stably degraded 100 mg/L indole but did not effectively remove skatole under the same strategy. Abstract-level MAG and transcript evidence implicated Bacteroidota, Chloroflexota, Desulfobacterota, and Methanobacterium populations in a candidate division of labor linking upstream indole oxidation, anthranilate-like aromatic-CoA processing, and methanogenesis-associated carbon flow.

name: Anammox Bioreactor DNRA Destabilization Community
description: A laboratory-scale anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox) bioreactor community followed from inoculation through a performance destabilization event and back to robust steady-state operation, characterized by metagenomics. Metabolic analyses showed selection for nutrient-acquisition capacities in the core community. Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) was the primary nitrogen-removal pathway that competed with anammox, and increased replication of DNRA-capable bacteria out-competed anammox bacteria, causing the loss of nitrogen-removal capacity. The DNRA-capable bacteria were closely associated with the anammox bacterium and are considered part of the core microbial community, underscoring how bacteria that are otherwise core members can be detrimental.

name: Anammox Granule Metabolic Interaction Community
description: A laboratory-scale anammox granular-sludge bioreactor community reconstructed with genome-centric metagenomics and metatranscriptomics. Brocadia-affiliated anammox bacteria dominate nitrogen removal, while Chlorobi-affiliated and other heterotrophic bacteria recycle nitrate to nitrite, degrade EPS-derived peptides, and scavenge detrital products from anammox growth.

name: Angelarchaeales Thermoplasmata CuMMO Soil and Sediment Community
description: A soil and aquifer-sediment microbial community in which a newly defined Thermoplasmatota archaeal order, Ca. Angelarchaeales, encodes divergent copper membrane monooxygenases (CuMMOs). Twenty genomes from distinct archaeal species were recovered from grassland and hillslope soils and aquifer sediments. The CuMMO proteins resemble Nitrososphaerales (ammonia monooxygenase) enzymes more than bacterial CuMMOs and retain all functional residues required for monooxygenase activity. Angelarchaeales genomes are enriched in blue copper proteins (BCPs) including plastocyanin-like electron carriers and divergent nitrite reductase-like (nirK) 2-domain cupredoxin proteins, encode strong peptide and amino-acid uptake/degradation capacity, and share electron transport mechanisms with Nitrososphaerales. Angelarchaeales are abundant in some of the source environments.

name: ANME-SRB Marine Methane Seep Consortium
description: Natural marine methane-seep consortia in which anaerobic methanotrophic archaea (ANME) grow in syntrophic partnership with sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB). These structured aggregates couple anaerobic oxidation of methane to sulfate reduction, limiting methane release from ocean sediments. The interaction is frequently organized as multicellular consortia containing ANME archaeal cells and bacterial sulfate reducers, with genomic evidence supporting direct interspecies electron transfer from ANME to the SRB partner.

name: ANME/SRB Anaerobic Methanotrophic Syntrophic Consortia
description: Marine syntrophic consortia of anaerobic methanotrophic archaea (ANME) and sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) that couple the anaerobic oxidation of methane to sulfate reduction in marine sediments. Sediment-free enrichment cultures of three consortium types (ANME-1/Desulfofervidus, ANME-2a/Seep-SRB1, and ANME-2a+2c/Seep-SRB1+2) exhibited high dry conductance close to that of electrogenic biofilms. Cyclic voltammetry revealed redox activity and generator-collector measurements showed electron transport over micrometer-scale distances, establishing that the symbiosis uses redox conduction (consistent with multiheme cytochrome c) for direct interspecies electron transport between the archaeal and bacterial partners.

name: Apple Fire Blight A+N+P SynCom
description: A nine-member bacterial synthetic community assembled from three apple fire-blight biocontrol design groups: Streptomyces recifensis SN1E1 and Paenibacillus polymyxa AF2927 as direct anti-Erwinia amylovora strains, Labrys miyagiensis NBRC101365, Labrys okinawensis DSM18385, Novosphingobium mathurense SM117, Novosphingobium endophyticum EGI60015, and Terriglobus aquaticus 03SUJ4 as healthy apple network taxa, and Kitasatospora papulosa AF6313 plus Pseudomonas lundensis AB23 as pathway-associated strains. The full A+N+P mixture eliminated visible disease in Fuji apple fruit wounds, matched oxytetracycline at 1.67% disease severity in rose flowers, and reduced Erwinia amylovora TS3128 density in apple flower exudate during follow-up co-cultivation assays.

name: Arabidopsis Bacillus Biocontrol SynCom150
description: A 150-member bacterial synthetic community assembled from genome-sequenced isolates recovered from surface-sterilized Brassicaceae roots, nearly all Arabidopsis thaliana, and applied to Arabidopsis Col-0 plants in gamma-irradiated coconut-coir and MS-agar microcosms. The study used top-down dropout and add-in deconstruction to test SynCom subsets against the leaf pathogen Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000, resolving Bacillus and Pseudomonadota as protective components; follow-up halo assays, Bacillus-only inocula, leaf-recovery CFU assays, and Arabidopsis RNA-seq supported a model in which diverse rhizospheric Bacillus suppress Pto without requiring host immune activation.

name: Arabidopsis Coumarin Root SynCom
description: A hydroponic 22-member Arabidopsis root-isolate SynCom used to detect strain-level rhizosphere community shifts caused by phytoalexin, flavonoid, and coumarin exudates. Under iron deficiency, F6'H1-dependent catecholic coumarins suppress the coumarin-sensitive isolate Pseudomonas sp. Root329 through a peroxide-linked mechanism that contributes to the overall wild-type-like community profile.

name: Arabidopsis Phyllosphere SynCom7
description: A seven-strain reduced-complexity Arabidopsis phyllosphere SynCom used to test host genetic effects on microbiota composition.

name: Asgard Archaea Wetland Soil Methanogenesis-Substrate Community
description: A wetland soil community in which terrestrial Asgard archaea modulate potential methanogenesis substrates. Two complete genomes were reconstructed for soil-associated Atabeyarchaeia, a newly defined Asgard lineage, alongside a complete genome for Freyarchaeia. Metatranscriptomic data show in situ expression of [NiFe]-hydrogenases, pyruvate oxidation, Wood-Ljungdahl-pathway carbon fixation, amino acid metabolism, anaerobic aldehyde oxidation, hydrogen peroxide detoxification, and carbohydrate breakdown to acetate and formate. Soil-associated Asgard archaea are predicted to act as non-methanogenic acetogens, suggesting that they modulate wetland-soil methanogenesis substrate pools (H2, acetate, formate) and shape terrestrial carbon cycling.

name: At-RSPHERE SynCom
description: A synthetic bacterial community derived from the Arabidopsis root microbiota culture collection (At-RSPHERE), representing 16 bacterial families isolated from Arabidopsis thaliana roots grown in natural soil. This community was established to study plant-microbe interactions and their effects on plant productivity and carbon cycling in the rhizosphere. The consortium members were selected to represent a broad taxonomic range covering the major bacterial phyla (Proteobacteria, Actinobacteria, and Bacteroidetes) found in the Arabidopsis root microbiome. Assembly sizes vary from 5-20 members depending on experimental design, enabling reductionist studies of root microbiota assembly and function.

name: Australian Lead Zinc Polymetallic Tailings Consortium
description: A sulfidic mine-tailings community model centered on a weathered volcanogenic massive sulfide dump in arid Western Australia and related Pb-Zn tailings acidification studies. Oxidative weathering of S- and Fe-rich waste rock disperses mobile ions including zinc, sulfur, chloride, and aluminium, while Pb-Zn tailing impoundments at progressive acidification stages contain Acidithiobacillus, Leptospirillum, and Ferroplasma acidophiles associated with iron oxidation, sulfur oxidation, carbon fixation, nitrogen fixation, and acid mine drainage generation. The curated causal graph therefore represents acidophile-driven Fe/S oxidation, Pb-Zn tailings acidification, and pH-ordered community succession as community-level processes rather than unsupported species-by-species exchanges.

name: Auxenochlorella-Pseudomonas Florfenicol Phycosphere Coculture
description: A defined freshwater green-alga and bacterium co-culture pairing axenic Auxenochlorella pyrenoidosa with Pseudomonas_sp1, a phycospheric isolate recovered after high-florfenicol and polylactic acid microplastic stress. Liu et al. isolated Pseudomonas_sp1 from the stressed phycosphere and used the isolate in short co-culture validation experiments showing promoted A. pyrenoidosa growth and Pseudomonas-associated pyridoxal production under florfenicol stress.

name: Avena Rhizosphere and Detritusphere Niche-Differentiated Decomposer Guilds
description: A rhizosphere and detritusphere microbial community of Avena fatua characterized by time-resolved metatranscriptomics across rhizosphere, detritusphere, and combined rhizosphere-detritusphere habitats. Transcripts were binned using a unique reference database from soil isolate genomes, single-cell amplified genomes, metagenomes, and stable-isotope-probing metagenomes. Soil habitat significantly affected both community composition and overall gene expression, but the succession of microbial functions occurred faster than compositional change. Hierarchical clustering of upregulated decomposition genes resolved four microbial guilds whose functional succession patterns suggest specialization for fresh growing roots, decaying root detritus, the combination of live and decaying root biomass, or aging root material. Carbohydrate depolymerization genes were consistently upregulated in the rhizosphere.

name: Avena Rhizosphere Cross-Kingdom 13C-SIP Community
description: A rhizosphere community of Avena fatua traced with stable isotope probing (SIP) by growing the plant in a 13CO2 atmosphere. Paired rhizosphere and nonrhizosphere soils sampled at 6 and 9 weeks were density-fractionated and sequenced to recover 55 bacterial genomes (>=70 percent complete), complete 18S rRNA sequences of 13C-enriched microeukaryotic bacterivores and fungi, and 10 circularized bacteriophage genomes. Some phages were the most labeled entities in the rhizosphere, suggesting phage are important agents of turnover of plant-derived carbon in soil. CRISPR spacer targeting linked one phage to a Burkholderiales host predicted to be a plant pathogen and another to a Catenulispora sp. predicted to be a plant growth-promoting bacterium. Heavily 13C-labeled bacterial genes include those involved in modulating plant signaling hormones, plant pathogenicity, and defense against microeukaryote grazing.

name: Bacillales Lignin-Degrading LDSynCom
description: An engineered eleven-strain Bacillales synthetic community assembled for aerobic beechwood-lignin degradation in M9 minimal medium. Zhou et al. 2026 screened a 121-strain Bacillales collection with a bottom-up clear-halo lignin-utilization assay and a top-down M9-lignin enrichment, distilled 15 candidates with crystal-violet biofilm and methylene-blue/Azure-B dye-decolorization assays, and retained 11 strains for the lignin-degrading SynCom. The final LDSynCom formed biofilms on lignin particles, accumulated more Folin-Ciocalteu-reactive phenolics than uninoculated and 11B-dropout controls, and produced extracellular proteomes whose lignin-induced proteins included Paenibacillus sp. 11B ring-cleaving dioxygenase candidates.

name: Bacillus A1-A3 Naphthalene Biofilm Consortium
description: A defined two-isolate Bacillus consortium, Consortium 3, assembled from Bacillus paranthracis isolate A1 and Bacillus licheniformis isolate A3 after enrichment of petroleum-contaminated soil from Ras Gharib, Egypt on polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. The A1/A3 pair was one of four consortia built from the three strongest phenanthrene- and naphthalene-degrading isolates. Consortium 3 was induced to grow as a glass-attached biofilm, showed the highest reported synergistic interaction during planktonic naphthalene degradation, reached 94.69% naphthalene degradation as a biofilm culture, and its preformed biofilm degraded 81.47% of naphthalene in artificially contaminated soil. Phenanthrene behaved differently: individual isolates outperformed the consortia, and the authors attributed the lower consortium rates to antagonistic interactions under the more complex PAH substrate.

name: Bacillus and Aspergillus Lignocellulose-Degrading Co-Vermicomposting SynCom
description: Synthetic lignocellulose-degrading cross-kingdom microbial consortium (SynCom) composed of Bacillus licheniformis, Bacillus subtilis, Aspergillus nidulans, and Aspergillus rugulosus applied at 5% inoculation during earthworm (Eisenia fetida) co-vermicomposting of high-lignin green waste and cattle manure. The SynCom stimulates lignocellulolytic enzyme and urease activities, enriches carbohydrate esterases, glycosyltransferases, and nitrification gene hao, reduces the C/N ratio, and increases humic substance and nitrate nitrogen content.

name: Bacillus and Pseudomonas Antagonistic Synthetic Community T7 Against Chili Root Rot
description: Synthetic bacterial community (T7 SynCom) constructed from core antagonistic rhizosphere biomarker isolates of Bacillus and Pseudomonas depleted during prolonged continuous cropping of chili pepper (Capsicum annuum). T7 SynCom directly antagonizes the root rot pathogen Fusarium solani, reduces chili root rot incidence, and induces systemic plant resistance by activating MAPK, ethylene, jasmonic acid, and salicylic acid immune signaling pathways.

name: Bacillus G12-Y4-X25 Tobacco Biocontrol SynCom
description: A three-member Bacillus synthetic microbial community assembled from Bacillus amyloliquefaciens G12, Bacillus pumilus Y4, and Bacillus velezensis X25 to combine complementary antagonistic activities against Fusarium oxysporum and Phytophthora nicotianae, the causal agents of tobacco Fusarium root rot and black shank. G12 was isolated from the tobacco rhizosphere and the Y4 and X25 endophytes from tobacco tissues in Luoyang, China. The strains showed only mild mutual inhibition in pairwise plate confrontations, the 1:1:1 SynCom produced more indole-3-acetic acid than any single strain, and glasshouse and two-site field assays linked the consortium to reduced soil-borne disease, improved tobacco root traits, and higher middle-leaf-based estimated yield.

name: Bacillus siamensis-vallismortis HT Masson Pine SynCom
description: A two-strain HT synthetic plant growth-promoting rhizobacterial community assembled from Trichoderma koningiopsis-conditioned Pinus massoniana rhizosphere isolates. The community combines Bacillus siamensis RW5 and Bacillus vallismortis RW8 and was tested against Fusarium oxysporum damping-off in Masson pine seedlings. Relative to the pathogen challenge control, HT reduced disease incidence by 36.67%, increased seedling height by 9.44%, enhanced protective enzyme activity, alleviated membrane damage, and activated the resistance genes PR1, FLS2, and CAT1.

name: Bacillus-Bradyrhizobium Straw Humification SynCom
description: A two-member Bacillus siamensis and Bradyrhizobium japonicum SynCom that promotes maize straw humification and soil organic carbon.

name: Bacillus-Pseudomonas Galveston PET Consortium
description: A naturally occurring five-member bacterial consortium isolated from petroleum-polluted coastal soil in Galveston Bay, Texas, and examined for polyethylene terephthalate (PET) biodegradation in carbon-free basal medium with PET granules or MHET. The consortium contains Bacillus thuringiensis 9.1, Bacillus cereus 13.1, and Pseudomonas species strains 9.2, 10, and 13.2. Integrated comparative genomics, secreted-proteome profiling, HPLC, and LC-MS analyses support a distributed PET-degradation model in which Bacillus strains contribute more strongly to extracellular hydrolysis, polymer-surface association, and persistence, while Pseudomonas strains contribute more strongly to aromatic transport, redox balancing, and downstream assimilation of PET-derived intermediates.

name: Bacillus-Saccharomyces Daqu Spatial-Cooperation SynCom
description: A Bacillus-Saccharomyces synthetic consortium used as a representative Daqu solid-state fermentation model for starch-mediated spatial cooperation. Temporal transcriptomics connected Bacillus-dominated starch hydrolysis with Saccharomyces-driven ethanol production across fermentation stages, fluorescently labeled synthetic consortia showed that starch availability governed colony expansion and spatial cooperation, and an engineered consortium carrying an IPTG-inducible alpha-amylase expression system was applied in Daqu fermentation to improve starch conversion efficiency and flavor compound formation.

name: Bacteroides-Desulfovibrio Carrageenan H2S Coculture
description: A defined in vitro two-species human-gut bacterial coculture in which Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron degrades carrageenan, releases inorganic sulfate, and fuels dissimilatory sulfate reduction and hydrogen sulfide production by Desulfovibrio desulfuricans.

name: Bacteroides-Eubacterium Gnotobiotic Gut Model
description: A defined two-member gnotobiotic mouse gut model pairing the human gut Bacteroidetes member Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482 with the human gut Firmicutes member Eubacterium rectale ATCC 33656. The model was used to examine niche specialization and metabolic interaction between dominant human gut phyla under controlled host and diet conditions. B. thetaiotaomicron expands polysaccharide utilization and host mucin glycan foraging in the presence of E. rectale, while E. rectale shifts away from glycan-degrading enzymes toward amino acid and sugar transport, glycolytic support, and butyrate generation from acetate.

name: Bacteroides-Methanobrevibacter Gnotobiotic Mouse Mutualism
description: A defined host-associated gnotobiotic mouse community used to test archaeal-bacterial mutualism in the gut. Germ-free mice were colonized with Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron with or without Methanobrevibacter smithii or Desulfovibrio piger, revealing a specific interaction in which M. smithii redirects B. thetaiotaomicron toward dietary fructan fermentation to acetate while using B. thetaiotaomicron formate for methanogenesis.

name: Baia de Todos os Santos Mangrove Alkane-Degrading Consortium
description: A petroleum-contaminated mangrove bacterial consortium from Baia de Todos os Santos, Brazil, reported as a 36-organism consortium and represented by nine selected Bacillus, Brevibacillus, Pseudomonas, and Stenotrophomonas isolates. de Santana Nazare et al. sequenced and compared the nine isolates, grew them in Bushnell-Haas broth with paraffinic crude oil, and found that the complete consortium was required for statistically significant intermediate n-alkane degradation while Pseudomonas/Stenotrophomonas and Bacillus members occupied rapid and delayed alkane-degradation roles.

name: Baijiu Pit Mud Hexanoic Acid SynCom G4
description: An ethanol-fed, hexanoic-acid-producing synthetic community constructed from Chinese baijiu fermentation pit mud using a top-down strategy. The G4 SynCom was dominated by Clostridium sensu stricto 12, described as primarily Clostridium kluyveri with an 86% value, with Clostridium sensu stricto 18 and Pseudoclavibacter also reported among dominant prokaryotes. Functional predictions and fermentation profiling suggested a potential association between G4 hexanoic acid production and reverse beta-oxidation; under optimized pH 7.9, 37.6 C, 8.2% inoculum, and 77% loading-volume conditions, SynCom G4 reached 4.69 g/L hexanoic acid.

name: Banana Fusarium Wilt Biocontrol SynCom1.2
description: A three-member banana rhizosphere SynCom designed for biological control of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense tropical race 4.

name: Barley DT Rhizosphere SynCom
description: A defined sixteen-strain drought-tolerant bacterial synthetic community assembled from barley-rhizosphere isolates collected at the Global Change Experimental Facility in Bad Lauchstadt. Rigerte et al. selected isolates with overlapping 16S rDNA sequences to drought- or future-climate-associated amplicon sequence variants, cultured the barley isolate set on YME agar, combined equal proportions of the sixteen single-strain suspensions, and applied the Barley DT-SynCom to barley seedlings before Blumeria graminis f. sp. hordei challenge and pre-challenge rhizosphere multi-omics assays.

name: Bayan Obo REE Tailings Consortium
description: An acid-producing bacterial consortium engineered to extract rare earth elements (REE) from tailings at the Bayan Obo mine in Inner Mongolia, China, the world's largest rare earth deposit. This functional bacterial consortium achieves exceptional REE recovery rates of 82-83% for the five main light rare earth elements (La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm) after 18 days of bioleaching using one-step or two-step processes. The tailings are iron extraction residues from medium-poor oxidized ores containing bastnaesite (REE(CO₃)F) and monazite as primary REE minerals. The consortium employs acid-producing bacteria including actinomycetes (Streptomyces sp.), autotrophic acidophiles (Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans), and heterotrophic acidophiles (Acidiphilium cryptum) that work synergistically to mobilize REE through acidolysis and organic acid complexation. Key mechanisms include production of organic acids (citric, oxalic, lactic, pyruvic), siderophores, and complexing ligands that solubilize REE from carbonate-fluoride minerals. The two-step process (sequential inoculation with heterotrophs followed by autotrophs) achieves 83.51% recovery versus 82.78% for one-step (simultaneous inoculation), demonstrating synergistic enhancement through pH control and organic acid accumulation. This system represents a critical sustainable biotechnology for recovering strategic REE materials essential for clean energy technologies, permanent magnets, and electronics while remediating millions of tons of existing Bayan Obo tailings.

name: Bifidobacterium breve-Trichomonas vaginalis Vaginal Co-culture
description: A defined two-member co-culture of the vaginal commensal Bifidobacterium breve with the sexually transmitted protozoan parasite Trichomonas vaginalis, assayed against HeLa epithelial cells. The result runs counter to the expectation that a beneficial commensal antagonises the parasite: over 4 h the protozoan proliferated 1.2-fold more while bacterial abundance fell 27%, microscopy showed direct physical association between the two organisms, and transcriptomics of T. vaginalis showed upregulation of fatty acid metabolism and DNA replication genes together with virulence-associated genes including adhesins, corroborated by metabolomic changes in long-chain fatty acids. B. breve conferred no protection on host epithelial cells, and the effects on the parasite were transient. The record captures a commensal-parasite association in which the commensal is depleted while the parasite is enhanced.

name: Bifidobacterium longum DSM20219 and Bacillus subtilis SOM8 Alginate Biofilm Probiotic Co-Culture
description: Engineered probiotic co-culture of oxygen-sensitive anaerobic Bifidobacterium longum DSM20219 and biofilm-forming Bacillus subtilis SOM8 co-encapsulated in sodium alginate hydrogel beads. Bacillus subtilis SOM8 promotes interspecies cell aggregation, extracellular polymeric matrix development, and biofilm formation within the alginate matrix, enhancing B. longum DSM20219 survival by ~3-log CFU/g (>7-log CFU/g) in simulated gastric and intestinal fluids and maintaining >6-log CFU/g over 28 days of aerobic storage.

name: Bifidobacterium-Faecalibacterium 2′-FL/FOS Butyrate Coculture
description: Defined two-strain anaerobic gut coculture containing Bifidobacterium bifidum JCM1254 and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii A2-165 (JCM31915). The strains were grown in 48-well batch cultures of sugar- and volatile-fatty-acid-free YCFA broth supplied with 0.5% total carbohydrate as 2′-fucosyllactose, fructooligosaccharides, or mixtures of the two. Monocultures showed B. bifidum responding to 2′-FL-rich substrates and F. prausnitzii growing in FOS-containing conditions; in the two-member coculture, total OD600 and lactate/acetate accumulation increased under 2′-FL-rich conditions, but butyrate peaked specifically at 10% 2′-FL plus 90% FOS, indicating ratio-dependent substrate complementarity and metabolite-mediated interaction.

name: Bifidobacterium-Ruminococcus Infant HMO Cross-Feeding Coculture
description: An infant gut microbiome cross-feeding system reconstructed from individualized cultivations with three infant fecal inocula and supplemented with the human milk oligosaccharide 2'-fucosyllactose (2'FL). Bifidobacterium breve typically cannot metabolize 2'FL on its own, but extracellular fucosidases encoded by coexisting Ruminococcus gnavus release lactose from 2'FL and unlock extensive B. breve growth. Targeted cocultures and supplementation of R. gnavus into an infant microbiome showed that R. gnavus promotes B. breve growth through HMO breakdown, demonstrating that infant HMO utilization depends on synergistic interactions among coexisting species.

name: BioAsteroid ISS Chondrite Biomining Consortium
description: The BioAsteroid experiment tested microbial biomining of asteroidal (L-chondrite) material under microgravity aboard the International Space Station (ISS). Two heterotrophic microorganisms — the bacterium Sphingomonas desiccabilis CP1D and the fungus Penicillium simplicissimum DSM 1078 — were flown both as single strains and as an artificial two-member consortium on crushed Northwest Africa (NWA) 869 L-chondrite meteorite fragments, in a 50% v/v R2A medium, inside BioMining Reactors housed in KUBIK incubators. The study measured leaching of 44 elements (including the platinum-group elements ruthenium, palladium and platinum, and other elements of industrial interest) from the meteorite and compared microbial versus abiotic (non-biological) leaching under microgravity and terrestrial gravity. Penicillium simplicissimum was the most effective bioleaching organism in microgravity, enhancing release of palladium, platinum and other elements relative to non-biological controls, while Sphingomonas desiccabilis formed a contiguous biofilm on the rock surface but performed similarly or worse than the abiotic control for most platinum-group elements. In the consortium, the fungus alone outperformed the mixture for palladium, suggesting an antagonistic effect of the bacterium. Metabolomic analysis showed distinct, microgravity-dependent changes in microbial metabolism, particularly for P. simplicissimum, with increased production of carboxylic acids and other molecules of potential biomining or pharmaceutical interest. The work demonstrates proof of principle for microbe-driven transformation of asteroidal material for in situ resource utilization in space.

name: BioModels MODEL1806250003 Spittlebug Sulcia-Sodalis Symbiosis
description: BioModels record MODEL1806250003 is a multi-compartment metabolic model of the spittlebug Philaenus spumarius and its bacterial endosymbionts Sulcia and Sodalis.

name: BioModels MODEL1806250004 Sharpshooter Sulcia-Baumannia Symbiosis
description: BioModels record MODEL1806250004 is a multi-compartment metabolic model of the sharpshooter Graphocephala coccinea and its bacterial endosymbionts Sulcia and Baumannia.

name: BioModels MODEL1806250005 Cicada Sulcia-Hodgkinia Symbiosis
description: BioModels record MODEL1806250005 is a multi-compartment metabolic model of the cicada Neotibicen canicularis and its bacterial endosymbionts Sulcia and Hodgkinia.

name: BioModels MODEL2204300001 Kefir Community Model
description: BioModels record MODEL2204300001 is a genome-scale model from the Blasche et al. kefir study and is described as a model of a microbial species participating in a kefir community.

name: BioModels MODEL2209060002 D pigrum - S aureus Community
description: BioModels record MODEL2209060002 is a community GEM combining Dolosigranulum pigrum and Staphylococcus aureus to emulate interactions in a human nasal-like environment.

name: BioModels MODEL2310020001 Mouse Metaorganism Model
description: BioModels record MODEL2310020001 contains an integrated metabolic metaorganism model of aging mice that connects a merged mouse gut microbiome metabolic model to colon, liver, and brain host-tissue models through gut lumen and bloodstream exchange compartments.

name: BioModels MODEL2405300001 Infant Gut HMO SynCom
description: BioModels record MODEL2405300001 contains genome-scale metabolic models used to study a synthetic human infant gut microbial community in the context of human milk oligosaccharides.

name: BioModels MODEL2407300002 Sponge Holobiont Network
description: BioModels record MODEL2407300002 provides simulations and model assets for an eight-species sponge microbiome network, modeling interactions among symbiont clades in a Stylissa holobiont.

name: BioRock ISS Basalt Biomining Consortium
description: A defined three-species bacterial panel flown as the ESA BioRock experiment on board the International Space Station to test microbial bioleaching of economically important elements from basaltic rock under microgravity, simulated Mars gravity, and simulated Earth gravity (with ground 1 x g controls). Sphingomonas desiccabilis CP1D (DSM 16792), Bacillus subtilis NCIB 3610 (DSM 10), and Cupriavidus metallidurans CH34 (DSM 2839) were each cultivated on slides of olivine basalt (collected near Gufunes, Reykjavik, Iceland; chosen as an analogue of Moon/Mars surface material) inside a purposely designed miniature biomining reactor housed in the KUBIK incubator. Sphingomonas desiccabilis enhanced mean leached concentrations of rare earth elements (the lanthanides plus yttrium) relative to non-biological controls in all gravity regimes, while Bacillus subtilis reduced REE bioleaching efficacy and Cupriavidus metallidurans showed no difference, demonstrating the microbial specificity of the process as on Earth. A companion analysis showed that Sphingomonas desiccabilis and Bacillus subtilis both enhanced vanadium leaching by 184.92 to 283.22% relative to sterile controls, and a third study found no significant differences in final bacterial cell concentrations between gravity regimes. Gravity level had no significant effect on mean leaching in any case, establishing the principle of biomining and associated bioindustrial processes on Solar System bodies with non-1 x g gravity.

name: Black Soldier Fly Larvae Gut SynCom (Bacillus + Lactobacillus + Issatchenkia)
description: A tripartite synthetic microbial community (SynCom) engineered from the core gut microbiota of black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) to enhance protein bioconversion from organic wastes. The SynCom combines the bacteria Bacillus and Lactobacillus with the yeast Issatchenkia and was assembled and tested in germ-free (gnotobiotic) larval hosts using multi-omics. Bacillus provides direct proteolytic activity, whereas Lactobacillus and Issatchenkia are associated with improved protein-conversion performance and amino-acid metabolic responses. The tripartite SynCom showed the highest protein conversion performance and distinct spatiotemporal distribution along the gut pH gradient, increasing final larval protein content by 63%.

name: Black-Soil Glucose-Activated Herbicide-Mixture Degrading Synthetic Community
description: Simplified four-isolate bacterial synthetic community (SynCom) constructed from keystone taxa—Burkholderia-Caballeronia-Paraburkholderia complex, Rhodanobacter, and Achromobacter—identified in a natural microbial consortium enriched from herbicide-stressed agricultural black soil in Northeast China. Activated by glucose supplementation that fuels glycolytic and TCA cycle energy supply and environmental acidification, the SynCom co-metabolically degrades a recalcitrant mixture of nicosulfuron (97.27%), mesotrione (68.00%), and atrazine (22.91%) via enriched catabolic genes including atzF (allophanate hydrolase) and gst (glutathione S-transferase).

name: Bosea-Pseudomonas Dimethachlon-Degradation Consortium
description: A defined two-strain consortium reconstructed from the dimethachlon-enriched community JHJ-2. Bosea sp. S6 transforms dimethachlon into the toxic intermediate 3,5-dichloroaniline, and Pseudomonas sp. KH-1 consumes that intermediate, completing a sequential degradation and detoxification handoff.

name: Bothnian Bay GAC-Dependent CIET-SAO Consortium
description: A coastal-sediment-derived, granular-activated-carbon-dependent enrichment consortium serially transferred for about a decade from Bothnian Bay sediments. In anaerobic, acetate-fed cultures amended with granular activated carbon (GAC), the consortium couples syntrophic acetate oxidation to methane formation by moving electrons from the dominant electrogenic syntroph Candidatus Geosyntrophus acetoxidans through the GAC matrix to a Methanosarcina-related electrotrophic methanogen. Long-read metagenomics recovered 24 MAGs from the GAC-propagated enrichment, including MAGs for the core acetate-oxidizing and methanogenic partners plus GAC-enriched Lentimicrobium, Sedimentibacter, and Desulforhopalus lineages.

name: Brachypodium Young Root Rhizosphere EcoFAB Community
description: A young Brachypodium distachyon primary-root rhizosphere community analyzed at two spatially distinct zones (root tip and root base) using EcoFABs fabricated ecosystems and conventional pot and tube containers with natural soil. 16S rRNA gene analysis shows a strong rhizosphere effect with significant enrichment of OTUs belonging to Actinobacteria, Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes, and Proteobacteria, while community composition did not differ between root tips and root base or across growth containers. Bulk metagenomic functional analysis revealed enrichment of metabolic-pathway and root-colonization genes in root tips, whereas nutrient-limitation and environmental-stress genes were enriched in bulk soil, indicating root-driven gradients in labile carbon and nutrient availability.

name: Brocadia Low-Nitrogen Anammox Consortium
description: An operated anammox biofilter community subjected to sustained low-substrate nitrogen stress, where metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, co-occurrence networks, and SMETANA supported functional succession from Ca. Kuenenia toward a multispecies, transcriptionally active Ca. Brocadia assemblage with lower modeled resource overlap and complementary auxotrophies.

name: Buchnera-Serratia Cinara cedri Endosymbiont Consortium
description: A natural co-obligate aphid endosymbiont consortium in the cedar aphid Cinara cedri, composed of Buchnera aphidicola BCc and Serratia symbiotica SCc. Genome-based metabolic inference shows that Buchnera BCc has lost some ancestral nutritional functions, while Serratia SCc retains or takes over functions needed by the host-associated consortium, including shared tryptophan biosynthesis and broader metabolic complementation.

name: Burkholderia-Pseudomonas YB2 PET Degradation Consortium
description: A defined two-strain synthetic consortium, YB2, constructed from Burkholderia cepacia ZY1 and Pseudomonas harudinis G1B at an optimized 4:5 inoculation ratio to improve polyethylene terephthalate (PET) depolymerization and downstream PET-hydrolysis-product conversion. At pH 7.0 and 30 °C, YB2 reached 4.30% +/- 0.11% PET film mass loss after 3 days, outperformed the individual strains, released BHET, MHET, TPA, and ethylene glycol, and converted 96.4% of BHET plus 97.3% of MHET within 2 days.

name: Butyrivibrio fibrisolvens + Selenomonas ruminantium + Ruminococcus albus Lignocellulolytic Rumen Consortium
description: A synthetic lignocellulolytic bacterial consortium designed from six bovine rumen microbial strains to enhance lignocellulose degradation for biofuel and enzyme production. Genome-scale community metabolic models were used with flux-based parameters (pairwise metabolic assistance, PMA; growth support index, PGSI) to predict compatible, mutualistic pairs, which were validated in experimentally grown cocultures. The strongest pairwise enzymatic synergism was observed for Butyrivibrio fibrisolvens with Selenomonas ruminantium (a 41% increase in endoglucanase activity), and a three-membered community of B. fibrisolvens, S. ruminantium, and Ruminococcus albus showed synergistic activity across all lignocellulosic substrates, indicating strong metabolic interplay among compatible species.

name: Cable Bacteria beneath Photosynthetic Biofilm Sediment Community
description: A coastal sediment community in which long filamentous Desulfobulbaceae cable bacteria connect sulfide-rich deeper sediment to oxygen supplied near the sediment-water interface by an oxygenic photosynthetic biofilm. The system links sulfur oxidation, oxygen production, sulfide availability, and centimeter-scale long-distance electron transfer.

name: Calcium-Tomato Bacterial Wilt SynCom
description: A four-member tomato-root SynCom assembled from calcium-enriched antagonists to suppress Ralstonia solanacearum bacterial wilt. Bi et al. isolated Dyella japonica, Rhodanobacter glycinis, Paenibacillus polymyxa, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa from tomato roots after calcium chloride amendment, selected them because they antagonized R. solanacearum, were promoted by calcium or calcium-induced root metabolites, and encoded plant-growth-promoting traits, and mixed OD600-normalized LB-grown suspensions 1:1:1:1. In 96-well root-exudate co-culture assays, the SynCom plus exudates from 20 mM calcium-treated tomato seedlings reduced R. solanacearum density; in greenhouse soil, the SynCom combined with a reduced 100 mg Ca kg-1 soil dose dropped bacterial wilt incidence from 74.07% to 0%.

name: Caldibacillus-Clostridium Aerotolerant Cellulose Coculture
description: A designed two-member thermophilic coculture for aerotolerant cellulose conversion. The community pairs the cellulolytic strict anaerobe Clostridium thermocellum with the noncellulolytic facultative anaerobe Caldibacillus debilis GB1. C. debilis GB1 provides respiratory protection under oxidative conditions, enabling synergistic cellulose utilization and ethanogenic biofuel production under an aerobic atmosphere.

name: Caldicellulosiruptor Two-Species Hydrogen Coculture
description: A de novo constructed, continuous-flow, hydrogen-producing coculture pairing Caldicellulosiruptor saccharolyticus DSM 8903 with the strain reported as Caldicellulosiruptor kristjanssonii DSM 12137. The system was designed to test whether two extreme thermophilic sugar-fermenting Caldicellulosiruptor strains could stably coexist while converting glucose and xylose, major lignocellulosic hydrolysate sugars, to hydrogen-rich fermentation products.

name: California Grassland Precipitation Legacy Soil Community
description: A semiarid California Mediterranean-climate grassland soil microbial community studied under two field-imposed precipitation regimes (100 percent versus 50 percent of mean annual precipitation) and assayed during the first autumn rewet. Quantitative H2-18O stable-isotope-probing, 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, metagenomics, and metatranscriptomics revealed that reduced winter precipitation imposed a lasting legacy on community turnover: microbial growth declined by about one order of magnitude and mortality by about two orders of magnitude relative to ambient plots, lowering community growth efficiency (new biomass growth divided by respiration). Soil organic carbon shifted from microbial-necromass-derived lipid-, amino-sugar-, and protein-like compounds toward more oxidized lignin- and tannin-like plant detritus compounds. Meta-omics linked high-CGE communities to N-rich necromass consumption with elevated amino acid and peptidoglycan biosynthesis and aromatic compound degradation, while low-CGE communities had elevated carbohydrate metabolism and lipid turnover consistent with plant-detritus processing and membrane maintenance.

name: Candida parapsilosis Hospitalized Infant Gut Microbiome Community
description: An in situ infant gut microbiome study of Candida parapsilosis colonization in hospitalized infants, combining metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and metaproteomics. Infant-06 fecal samples recovered C. parapsilosis alongside Enterococcus faecalis, Lactobacillus gasseri, and Staphylococcus epidermidis; the time series placed Candida in an early low-complexity gut community, followed its replacement or outnumbering largely by E. faecalis, and linked Candida-positive samples to shifts in Enterococcus ribosomal and mannitol phosphotransferase-system transcript features.

name: Caragana korshinskii Cross-Kingdom Forage Bio-Valorization SynCom
description: A defined three-member, two-kingdom synthetic microbial community assembled to break the lignocellulose barrier of Caragana korshinskii, a shrub legume used as an arid-region feed resource. Lactobacillus plantarum supplies rapid acidification, Bacillus subtilis supplies fibrolytic enzyme secretion, and Aspergillus niger supplies what the source calls oxidative delignification potential. Against the control, the SynCom treatment reached higher in vitro dry matter digestibility (49.68%) and neutral detergent fibre digestibility (25.65%), shifted the silage microbiome so that Lactobacillus exceeded 95% of it, suppressed the spoilage genera Staphylococcus and Weissella by competitive exclusion, and upregulated predicted pyruvate metabolism and amino-acid biosynthesis. CURATION SCOPE. Only the abstract of the source is available: the paper is gold open access at the publisher but has no PMC deposit, Europe PMC serves no full text, and the publisher blocks programmatic retrieval, so references_cache/PMID_42432469.md is content_type abstract_only. Strain designations, inoculation rates, ensiling vessel, temperature, moisture and duration, control-arm values, pH and organic-acid data, sequencing methods and any sequence accessions are all unavailable and are therefore absent here because they were not readable, not because the study did not report them. Re-check with the Europe PMC search for EXT_ID:42432469 and curate the rest once a pmcid appears.

name: Caragana-Wheat Drought SynCom15
description: A fifteen-member bacterial synthetic community constructed from drought-responsive core microbes of the desert shrub Caragana korshinskii and tested as a cross-host wheat drought-tolerance inoculant. Hao et al. combined four functional strains with eleven core microbial strains, assayed the full SynCom15 in potted plant experiments, and linked SynCom inoculation to wheat growth under drought, Pseudomonas-associated biofilm and quorum-sensing functions, and later streamlining into a biofilm-forming SynCom5.

name: Cellulomonas-Rhodobacter Cellulose Photohydrogen Coculture
description: A defined anaerobic cellulose-to-hydrogen coculture pairing cellulolytic Cellulomonas sp. strain ATCC 21399 with the purple nonsulfur phototroph Rhodopseudomonas capsulata, now classified as Rhodobacter capsulatus. The Cellulomonas partner ferments cellulose to organic acids, while R. capsulata grows photoheterotrophically on those products and evolves molecular hydrogen through nitrogenase. The system is DOE-relevant as an early model for lignocellulosic biohydrogen production by division of labor between cellulose fermentation and phototrophic hydrogen evolution.

name: Cellulose-to-Methane Combinatorial SynCom Panel
description: A bounded anaerobic synthetic-community panel assembled from the cellulolytic bacterium Ruminiclostridium cellulolyticum H10, the hydrogenotrophic methanogen Methanospirillum hungatei JF-1, the acetoclastic methanogen Methanosaeta concilii GP6, and the sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough. The experiment co-cultured all cellulose-fed bi-, tri-, and quad-species combinations containing R. cellulolyticum, plus the R. cellulolyticum monoculture, and used proteogenomics, stoichiometric flux modeling, and SMETANA to resolve context-dependent cross-feeding, competition, and methanogenic carbon flow.

name: Cellulose-to-Methane Quad-Culture SynCom
description: A four-species anaerobic synthetic community coupling cellulose degradation, sulfate reduction, and methanogenesis.

name: CeMbio Caenorhabditis elegans Microbiome
description: CeMbio is a defined, ecologically informed twelve-strain bacterial community representing the natural Caenorhabditis elegans microbiome. The v1.0 community includes Enterobacter hormaechei CEent1, Lelliottia amnigena JUb66, Acinetobacter guillouiae MYb10, Sphingomonas molluscorum JUb134, Stenotrophomonas indicatrix JUb19, Pseudomonas lurida MYb11, Pseudomonas berkeleyensis MSPm1, Comamonas piscis BIGb0172, Pantoea nemavictus BIGb0393, Ochrobactrum vermis MYb71, Sphingobacterium multivorum BIGb0170, and Chryseobacterium scophthalmum JUb44. The resource pairs a genetically tractable host with cultured, genome-sequenced, CGC-distributed commensal isolates that colonize the worm gut as a community, alter nematode developmental timing, and support follow-up behavioral and metabolic studies with the same reference composition.

name: Cheese Rind In Situ-In Vitro Model Community
description: A tractable fermented-food surface biofilm system based on cheese rind microbial communities. Wolfe and colleagues surveyed 137 rind communities across 10 countries, isolated representatives of the dominant bacterial and fungal genera, and reconstructed simplified cheese-curd-agar communities in vitro to test how moisture, washing, pH, and bacterial-fungal interactions shape reproducible community assembly and succession.

name: Chicken BL6 Anti-Salmonella SynCom
description: A defined six-strain synthetic consortium, BL6, assembled from Wenchang and Danzhou chicken gut isolates with in vitro anti-Salmonella activity. The consortium contains Bacillus velezensis CMLH125, Ligilactobacillus salivarius CMLH112, novel Bacillus sp. CMLH124, Lactobacillus johnsonii CMLH106, Lactobacillus crispatus CMLH109, and Lactobacillus gallinarum CMLH110. The strains were normalized after 72 h of cultivation, combined in equal proportions, washed, and resuspended in PBS with 20% glycerol for oral gavage of 1-day-old chicks before Salmonella Typhimurium challenge. In the chick model, BL6 mitigated Salmonella-associated intestinal injury, helped maintain barrier and liver function, reduced systemic inflammatory responses, and favored sustained Lactobacillus enrichment in the ileal microbiota.

name: Chinese Distillers Grains Dual Fungal Lignin Consortium
description: A two-member fungal solid-state fermentation system consisting of Phanerochaete chrysosporium and Pleurotus eryngii that was constructed to convert the recalcitrant lignin fraction of Chinese Distillers' grains. Chen et al. 2026 measured 58.66% lignin degradation in Chinese Distillers' grains, day-10 peaks in laccase and manganese peroxidase activity, a day-15 peak in lignin peroxidase activity, and transcriptomic/metabolomic evidence that P. chrysosporium was most active in early oxidative lignin cleavage while P. eryngii became dominant during later aromatic catabolism.

name: Chlamydomonas-Bacterial Hydrogen Production Consortium
description: A synthetic algae-bacteria consortium for sustainable hydrogen production, composed of the green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii and three bacterial species: Microbacterium forte sp. nov., Bacillus cereus, and Stenotrophomonas goyi sp. nov. This mutualistic association produces up to 313 mL H2/L over 17 days in high-cell density cultures. M. forte is the primary bacterial species responsible for improving algal hydrogen production, while the complete bacterial community enhances and sustains photobiological H2 generation through metabolic cooperation.

name: Chlamydomonas-Methylobacterium Mutualistic Consortium
description: A two-member mutualistic consortium consisting of the green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii and the methylotrophic bacterium Methylobacterium aquaticum, isolated from a freshwater environment. This natural association demonstrates reciprocal metabolic exchange under nitrogen stress conditions, mediated by indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) signaling. The alga provides photosynthetically fixed carbon and oxygen, while Methylobacterium modulates IAA levels through both production and degradation, influencing algal physiology and stress responses. This system serves as a model for understanding algae-bacteria interactions in freshwater ecosystems and potential applications in sustainable algal biotechnology under nutrient limitation.

name: Chlorella fusca CHK0059 Keystone-Taxa Antifungal SynCom
description: A four-isolate bacterial synthetic community selected from Chlorella-associated plant microbiome networks: Pseudomonas 8C3D12, Pseudoduganella rivuli FT92W (KACC 21474), Pseudomonas 6C7F4 and Brevibacterium renqingii REN4 (KCTC 49366). The two Pseudomonas isolates share a genus-level taxonomy entry here; three bacterial taxonomy entries do not mean three isolates. Table 1 distinguishes the network label Duganella from the inoculated Pseudoduganella strain. Treat8 combines all four bacteria with Fusarium challenge; Treat9 also contains C. fusca CHK0059. Host disease-index responses depend on treatment, host and time, without demonstrated universal superiority to single isolates or formal synergy. Separate in-vitro strawberry rhizosphere microbiome-fraction assays show compositional responses to live/killed Chlorella, methanol extract and mannitol. Algal mannitol secretion, strain-specific recruitment and the mechanism mediating plant protection remain unresolved. The 2025 precursor names Rhizomicrobium rather than Brevibacterium as its third correlated genus; the two studies do not establish identical keystone sets.

name: Chlorella vulgaris Whey Co-culture
description: A defined microalgal co-culture pairing the Chlorella vulgaris culture abbreviated CVB with Chlorella vulgaris CCAP 211/19 in casein whey-based media for dairy-whey valorization. Kelarijani et al. 2026 reported that the Chlorella vulgaris co-culture exhibited synergistic growth relative to single cultures and to a four-species algal mix in the casein whey panel.

name: Chlorella-Azospirillum Synthetic Mutualism
description: A defined algal-bacterial synthetic mutualism pairing the freshwater green microalga Chlorella sorokiniana UTEX 2714 with the plant-growth-promoting bacterium Azospirillum brasilense Cd. The pair has been studied in co-immobilized alginate bead systems and related culture formats to test how nutrient availability shapes mutualistic population growth, tryptophan, thiamine, and indole-3-acetic acid exchange, starch accumulation, and algal-bacterial aggregation. The system is relevant to environmental biotechnology, microalgal biomass production, and algal-bacterial interaction design.

name: Chlorella-Ecoli Mixotrophic Biofuel Precursor Coculture
description: A defined algal-bacterial coculture in which Chlorella minutissima was grown with Escherichia coli in airlift reactors under mixotrophic glucose, glycerol, and acetate conditions. The coculture produced more algal biomass, consumed more carbon substrate, and increased lipid and starch productivity relative to axenic algal cultures. This system is relevant to DOE-aligned algal biofuel biotechnology because it tests whether bacterial contamination or partnership can improve production of algal biofuel precursors rather than suppressing algal biomass.

name: Chlorella-Rhizobium Bioflocculation
description: A co-culture system pairing the microalgae Chlorella vulgaris with the bioflocculant-producing bacterium Rhizobium radiobacter F2 for enhanced algal harvesting in wastewater treatment applications. The bacterium produces extracellular polysaccharide bioflocculants that induce aggregation and flocculation of algal cells, enabling efficient biomass recovery for biofuel production. This bioflocculation approach avoids the negative effects of traditional chemical flocculants and provides a cost-effective, environmentally friendly method for microalgae harvesting, with flocculation efficiency improving from 0.2% (axenic algae) to >90% with bacterial co-culture.

name: Chlorochromatium aggregatum Phototrophic Consortium
description: A structured freshwater phototrophic bacterial consortium in which one central motile heterotrophic beta-proteobacterium, Candidatus Symbiobacter mobilis, is surrounded by approximately 15 green sulfur bacterial Chlorobium chlorochromatii epibionts. Genome analyses support a highly specialized symbiosis involving metabolite exchange, central-bacterium sensing and motility toward light and sulfide, cell-cell adhesion, and possible quinone-mediated electron exchange.

name: Choysum SynLAV DEHP-Degrading Rhizobacterial SynCom
description: A five-member synthetic rhizobacterial community assembled from the low-accumulation choysum rhizosphere isolates Flavobacterium sp. L11, Pseudomonas sp. L29, Sphingomonas sp. L75, Rhodococcus sp. L44, and Gordonia sp. L115. The isolates were selected as non-antagonistic, DEHP-degrading representative strains, mixed at equal ratios after OD600 0.5 normalization, and tested in choysum pots containing 100 mg/kg DEHP-contaminated soil.

name: Chromium Sulfur Oxidation Enrichment
description: An enrichment consortium in which microbial chromate reduction is coupled to anaerobic oxidation of inorganic electron donors. A 60-day cultivation study showed that sludge enrichments supplied with elemental sulfur, S(0), or zerovalent iron, Fe(0), as sole electron donors biologically reduced Cr(VI), deposited Cr(III) as the main reduction product, and achieved high chromate removal in both independent donor systems. High-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing linked this transformation to a consortium-level division of labor in which S(0)- or Fe(0)-oxidizing bacteria such as Thiobacillus or Ferrovibrio generated volatile fatty acids that chromate-reducing bacteria such as Geobacter or Desulfovibrio could further use to reduce chromate.

name: CICC Three-Strain Probiotic M-MV Luteolin Consortium
description: Defined anaerobic co-culture of Bifidobacterium longum CICC25033, Clostridium butyricum CICC23847, and Limosilactobacillus reuteri CICC6131 used to produce mixed-species probiotic membrane vesicles (M-MVs). Hou et al. grew the strains singly, pairwise, and as a 1:1:1 three-strain combination in MRS broth, observed higher viable counts in co-culture and with cell-free supernatants from partner strains, isolated M-MVs from the supernatant of the co-culture, found a distinct M-MV proteomic profile with antioxidant activity, and loaded luteolin into the resulting M-MVs for in-vitro and DSS-induced mouse-colitis assays.

name: Cinnamate β-Oxidation Consortium
description: A syntrophic 3-member anaerobic consortium for degradation of cinnamate via β-oxidation to benzoate, consisting of Papillibacter cinnamivorans, Syntrophus sp., and Methanobacterium formicicum. P. cinnamivorans performs β-oxidation of cinnamate to benzoate, followed by syntrophic benzoate degradation by Syntrophus sp. to acetate, H2, and CO2, with the methanogen consuming H2 to produce methane. This stepwise aromatic compound degradation pathway is important for anaerobic bioremediation.

name: Clostridial isoDCA Mini Consortium
description: A two-member engineered Clostridia consortium pairing Peptacetobacter hiranonis with Ruminococcus gnavus VPI C7-9 WT so the community converts host-derived taurocholic acid through cholic acid and deoxycholic acid to isodeoxycholic acid. Ionescu et al. also built a matched P. hiranonis plus R. gnavus KO consortium with rumgna_00694 disrupted as an isoDCA-negative control, enabling in vitro bile-acid conversion assays and antibiotic-treated mouse engraftment experiments that isolate the host effects of isoDCA.

name: Clostridium acetobutylicum and Clostridium ljungdahlii Carbon-Negative Isopropanol Syntrophic Coculture
description: High-cell-density syntrophic bacterial coculture pairing genetically engineered Clostridium acetobutylicum (CACas9 delta-hbd-p95ace02_atoB, lacking 4-C metabolism and overexpressing an acetone-formation pathway) with the acetogen and ketoreductase partner Clostridium ljungdahlii in a 3.6-L perfusion bioreactor. C. acetobutylicum ferments glucose to acetone, CO2, and H2; C. ljungdahlii consumes dissolved H2—relieving the thermodynamic bottleneck of NADH-driven H2 evolution in C. acetobutylicum—and reduces cross-fed acetone to isopropanol at supratheoretical yields in continuous carbon-negative glucose fermentation.

name: Clostridium acetobutylicum-Clostridium ljungdahlii Syntrophic Fusion Coculture
description: A defined two-member anaerobic coculture of the solventogen Clostridium acetobutylicum ATCC 824 and the acetogen Clostridium ljungdahlii DSM 13528. CO2 and H2 produced by C. acetobutylicum feed C. ljungdahlii, and the pairing also produces interspecies cell fusion with large-scale exchange of protein, RNA, and DNA between the two organisms. RNA sequencing of the coculture against the two monocultures, and of membrane-separated against unseparated cocultures in a transwell system, separates the effect of soluble signals from the effect of direct cell-to-cell contact. The transcriptional program shows differential regulation of the C. ljungdahlii Wood-Ljungdahl pathway and of the motility machinery, and of amino-acid biosynthesis and degradation; arginine and histidine made by C. acetobutylicum are proposed to be metabolized by C. ljungdahlii for extra ATP and carbon. The authors read the pairing as mutualistic rather than the commensalism previously assumed. This record is scoped to the WILD-TYPE pairing. The same laboratory has since reported much higher isopropanol and butanol titers from the same species pair using genetically modified C. acetobutylicum; those are properties of the engineered pairing and are deliberately not curated here.

name: Clostridium autoethanogenum-Clostridium kluyveri Syngas Coculture
description: A defined anaerobic synthetic coculture combining the acetogenic syngas fermenter Clostridium autoethanogenum with the chain-elongating bacterium Clostridium kluyveri. C. autoethanogenum converts carbon monoxide or syngas into acetate and ethanol, while C. kluyveri consumes these products for chain elongation, producing C4 and C6 fatty acids and higher alcohols. The system is relevant to DOE carbon utilization and renewable fuels because it couples gas fermentation with microbial upgrading of CO/syngas-derived intermediates in one growth vessel.

name: Clostridium carboxidivorans-Clostridium kluyveri CO Chain-Elongation Coculture
description: A defined anaerobic synthetic coculture pairing the autotrophic solventogenic acetogen Clostridium carboxidivorans with the chain-elongating bacterium Clostridium kluyveri. In CO/CO2-fed stirred-tank bioreactors, C. kluyveri elongates C2 products to organic acids, and C. carboxidivorans reduces those acids to longer-chain alcohols such as butanol and hexanol. The system is DOE-relevant because it couples waste-gas/syngas fermentation, carbon utilization, and production of liquid fuels and platform chemicals.

name: Clostridium cellulolyticum-Geobacter sulfurreducens Cellulose MFC Coculture
description: A defined binary microbial fuel cell coculture pairing the cellulolytic fermenter Clostridium cellulolyticum with the electrochemically active bacterium Geobacter sulfurreducens. The community couples cellulose hydrolysis and fermentation to anode respiration: C. cellulolyticum metabolizes cellulose, while G. sulfurreducens uses fermentation products to transfer electrons to the anode. The same exact two-species composition was reported in an initial cellulose-to-electricity study and a follow-up cellulose-fed microbial biofilm ecology study. The system is relevant to DOE bioenergy because it converts cellulosic biomass into electricity in a controlled bioelectrochemical reactor.

name: Clostridium cellulovorans-Beijerinckii AECC ABE Coculture
description: A defined anaerobic artificial symbiosis pairing the cellulolytic, butyrate-producing mesophile Clostridium cellulovorans 743B with the non-cellulolytic solventogenic bacterium Clostridium beijerinckii NCIMB 8052. The coculture was designed for consolidated bioprocessing of alkali extracted deshelled corn cobs, where C. cellulovorans saccharifies lignocellulose and produces butyric acid, and C. beijerinckii converts the released soluble sugars and butyric acid into acetone-butanol-ethanol solvents. The system is DOE-relevant as a lignocellulosic biomass-to-biofuel community model using an agricultural residue feedstock.

name: Clostridium cellulovorans-Methanosarcina barkeri Cellulose Methane Coculture
description: A defined anaerobic cellulose-to-methane coculture combining the cellulolytic fermenter Clostridium cellulovorans 743B with the metabolically versatile methanogen Methanosarcina barkeri Fusaro. C. cellulovorans degrades cellulose and produces methanogenesis precursors including hydrogen, formate, and acetate, while M. barkeri consumes those products for methanogenesis. The system is relevant to DOE bioenergy because it is an experimentally tractable model for renewable methane production from cellulosic biomass and for engineering anaerobic biomethanation consortia.

name: Clostridium cellulovorans-Rhodopseudomonas palustris Cellulose Biohydrogen Coculture
description: A defined two-member cellulose-to-biohydrogen coculture combining the cellulolytic dark-fermentative bacterium Clostridium cellulovorans 743B with the purple nonsulfur photosynthetic bacterium Rhodopseudomonas palustris CGA009. The coculture links cellulose degradation, volatile-fatty-acid exchange, pH stabilization, and photofermentative hydrogen production. It is DOE-relevant as a genetically tractable model for lignocellulosic bioenergy, integrated dark/photo fermentation, and mechanistic design of biohydrogen consortia.

name: Clostridium ljungdahlii-Clostridium kluyveri Syngas Alcohol Coculture
description: A defined anaerobic synthetic coculture that combines the acetogenic syngas fermenter Clostridium ljungdahlii with the chain-elongating bacterium Clostridium kluyveri in a continuously fed syngas bioprocess with in-line product extraction. C. ljungdahlii converts syngas into ethanol and acetate, while C. kluyveri uses ethanol for reverse-beta-oxidation chain elongation to butyrate and caproate. The same community also produced longer-chain alcohols including butanol, hexanol, and traces of octanol within a narrow pH range. The system is relevant to DOE carbon utilization and renewable fuels because it converts C1 gases into C4-C8 fuels and chemicals through microbial cross-feeding.

name: Clostridium phytofermentans-E. coli Cellobiose Biofilm Consortium
description: A rationally designed two-member artificial consortium composed of Clostridium phytofermentans ISDg, currently represented in NCBI Taxonomy as Lachnoclostridium phytofermentans ISDg, and Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655. The community was built to improve conversion of cellulose-derived sugars into ethanol, biomass, and other bioproduct-relevant outputs through division of labor between a cellulolytic obligate anaerobe and a facultative anaerobe. It is DOE-relevant because it models consolidated lignocellulosic bioprocessing, cellobiose conversion, biofilm oxygen partitioning, and cross-feeding mechanisms that can improve cellulosic fuel and chemical production.

name: Clostridium Thermocellum-Saccharoperbutylacetonicum Cellulosic Butanol Coculture
description: A staged two-member coculture for producing n-butanol from crystalline cellulose. The cellulolytic thermophile Clostridium thermocellum, represented in NCBI Taxonomy as Acetivibrio thermocellus ATCC 27405, first hydrolyzes Avicel cellulose. The butanol-producing Clostridium saccharoperbutylacetonicum strain N1-4 is then added for solvent production. The system is DOE-relevant because it couples consolidated cellulose deconstruction to cellulosic butanol production, a liquid biofuel and bioproduct target.

name: Clostridium-Caldicellulosiruptor Minimal Medium Coculture
description: A thermophilic, anaerobic, two-member laboratory coculture pairing Clostridium thermocellum ATCC 27405 with Caldicellulosiruptor bescii DSM 6725. The system was used to test whether low-ionic-strength defined medium with reduced nitrogen, sulfur, phosphate, and vitamin supplements could maintain both cellulolytic bacterial populations during conversion of cellulosic substrates relevant to consolidated bioprocessing.

name: Clostridium-E. coli-Nitratidesulfovibrio Minority-Mediator Consortium
description: A defined anaerobic three-strain consortium containing Clostridium acetobutylicum ATCC 824, Escherichia coli DH10B, and Nitratidesulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough NCIMB 8303. In glucose-yeast extract medium, the minority N. vulgaris population persists as a physical and metabolic mediator, reduces E. coli-associated inhibition of C. acetobutylicum growth, and can exchange cytoplasmic material with both other members.

name: Clostridium-Saccharomyces Cellulose Ethanol Coculture
description: A synthetic two-member cellulose-to-ethanol coculture pairing the cellulolytic mesophile Clostridium phytofermentans ISDg, currently represented in NCBI Taxonomy as Lachnoclostridium phytofermentans ISDg, with the engineered cellodextrin-fermenting yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae cdt-1. The consortium is maintained by controlled oxygen delivery: the yeast removes inhibitory oxygen and receives soluble sugars released during C. phytofermentans cellulose hydrolysis. With added endoglucanase, the coculture produced approximately 22 g/L ethanol from 100 g/L alpha-cellulose. This system is relevant to DOE lignocellulosic biofuel and consolidated bioprocessing goals.

name: Clostridium-Thermoanaerobacter Cellulosic Bioethanol Coculture
description: A thermophilic, anaerobic, two-member laboratory coculture for consolidated cellulosic bioethanol production.
