The community was identified through stress-induced enrichment analysis and validated across 12 soil types, demonstrating that keystone species recruitment can guide functional microbial community assembly to synergistically enhance plant health.

name: Urine Nitrification Synthetic Microbial Community
description: A five-member synthetic microbial community containing nitrifiers and ureolytic heterotrophs for urine nitrification.

name: Variovorax-Cryptococcus Vitamin Cross-Feeding Microcosm
description: A two-member vitamin cross-feeding microcosm derived from mine tailings laboratory microbial consortia, in which a Variovorax species produces thiamine (vitamin B1) as a community hub for correlated thiamine auxotrophs and a Cryptococcus yeast supplies pantothenate (vitamin B5) required by Variovorax. Co-culture of the two members yielded a 90-130 fold fitness increase for both organisms, supporting the bidirectional vitamin-dependent mutualism predicted from metagenome-informed abundance correlation networks of mine-tailings-derived consortia grown under dozens of conditions.

name: Viili Fungus-Bacterium EPS SynCom
description: A top-down three-strain synthetic microbial consortium from Viili fermented milk, composed of Lactococcus lactis V9, Lacticaseibacillus paracasei V21, and Geotrichum candidum Y1. Hu et al. 2026 used monoculture, co-culture, supernatant-supplementation, metabolomics, amino-acid depletion, amino-acid supplementation, and AI-2 perturbation assays to show that G. candidum supplies lactic-acid bacteria with nitrogen sources including valine, increases AI-2/luxS quorum-sensing activity, and gives the three-member community the highest measured exopolysaccharide concentration among the tested microbial combinations.

name: Waste-Sludge Electro-Fermentation Biofilm-Suspension Community
description: An engineered waste-activated-sludge electro-fermentation community with spatially differentiated electrode-biofilm and planktonic fractions. The source reports biofilm-associated reductive debromination of 4-bromophenol and suspension-associated acidogenesis for volatile-fatty-acid recovery. The five genera recorded here are enriched functional examples, not an exhaustive inventory of the sludge community.

name: Watermelon Rhizosphere Fusarium-Protective SynCom8
description: A simplified eight-member watermelon rhizosphere SynCom derived from an initial 16-member grafted-watermelon core community.

name: Wetland Lindane-Degrading Organochlorine Bacterial Consortium
description: Functional anaerobic organochlorine-degrading bacterial consortia (top-down consortium M and bottom-up consortium Y13) constructed around generalist non-obligate organochlorine-degrading Enterococcus strains (Enterococcus casseliflavus PseS3, R1, R3, R12) alongside organohalide-respiring and fermentative partners (Sulfurospirillum multivorans, Trichlorobacter lovleyi, Dehalococcoides mccartyi, and Petrimonas sulfuriphila) for gamma-hexachlorocyclohexane (lindane) bioremediation in coastal wetland sediment microcosms while suppressing CO2-reduction methanogenesis.

name: Wetland Oxygen-Sulfate Greenhouse Gas Microcosm Community
description: Freshwater wetland soil microbial microcosms incubated under anoxic non-sulfate, anoxic sulfate-addition, oxic non-sulfate, and oxic sulfate-addition conditions to resolve how climate-linked oxygen and sulfate exposures alter methane and carbon dioxide emissions. The study integrated geochemical measurements, proteogenomics, metaproteomics, and stoichiometric modeling to identify altered microbial guilds and metabolic processes driving CH4 and CO2 emissions. Sulfate exposure reduced methane production, oxygen shifted greenhouse gas emissions from CH4 toward CO2, and the combined exposure resembled oxygen exposure alone.

name: Wheat Crown-Rot Six-Strain Cross-Kingdom SMC
description: A six-strain cross-kingdom wheat-rhizosphere synthetic microbial community that combined Trichoderma harzianum T19, Bacillus subtilis BS-Z15, Bacillus spizizenii PM9, Bacillus rugosus PM16, Bacillus rugosus S32, and Bacillus halotolerans S8 for nonsterile-soil wheat pot assays against Fusarium pseudograminearum Fusarium crown rot. Zhou et al. 2026 assembled the SMC from antagonistic, growth-promoting, and auxiliary wheat-rhizosphere isolates and compared sterile-water, Fusarium-only, SMC-only, and SMC-plus-Fusarium treatments for plant growth, disease severity, resident rhizosphere amplicon profiles, co-occurrence networks, and rhizosphere metabolomics.

name: Wheat Crown-Rot TB Cross-Kingdom SynCom
description: A minimal two-member cross-kingdom wheat-rhizosphere SynCom, named TB by Zhou et al. 2026, that mixed Trichoderma harzianum T19 with Bacillus rugosus PM16 and was soil-drenched onto Fusarium-pseudograminearum-challenged Triticum aestivum cv. Hechun 213 seedlings. The controlled tissue-culture-chamber pot experiment tested sterile-water, Fusarium-only, SynCom-only, and Fusarium-plus-SynCom treatments in non-sterile topsoil; after 45 days the authors scored wheat crown rot, profiled rhizosphere 16S/ITS communities, and measured rhizosphere metabolites.

name: Wheat DT Rhizosphere SynCom
description: A defined sixteen-strain drought-tolerant bacterial synthetic community assembled from wheat-rhizosphere isolates collected at the Global Change Experimental Facility in Bad Lauchstadt. Rigerte et al. selected isolates with overlapping 16S rDNA sequences to drought- or future-climate-associated amplicon sequence variants, cultured the wheat isolate set on YME agar, combined equal proportions of the sixteen single-strain suspensions, and applied the Wheat DT-SynCom to barley seedlings before Blumeria graminis f. sp. hordei challenge and pre-challenge rhizosphere multi-omics assays.

name: Wheat Straw Biogas Pretreatment SynCom
description: A four-member bacterial-fungal synthetic microbial community that produces enzymes for wheat straw pretreatment and enhanced biogas production.

name: Wheat SynCom-SASW01 Drought-Resistance Inoculant
description: A five-strain bacterial synthetic community composed of Enterobacter hormaechei FN0603, Enterobacter cloacae FWP0601, Enterobacter ludwigii FWP1205, Pseudomonas putida FWP0405, and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia HLPD6. Yu et al. activated each stored strain on R2A agar, verified species identity by 16S rRNA V5-V7 sequencing, normalized the strains to OD600 1.0, and mixed the suspensions at an equal 1:1:1:1:1 ratio to assemble SynCom-SASW01. The study applied the consortium alone or as a biochar-based wheat seed coating under drought stress, then measured wheat growth, rhizosphere nutrients, root-associated microbiomes, antioxidant physiology, and dual-site field yield.

name: Wheat Synthetic Consortium C1
description: A four-member wheat-rhizosphere synthetic consortium (SynCom 1/C1) composed of Pseudomonas sp. B5, Pseudomonas sp. B11, Pseudomonas sp. B12, and Pseudomonas sp. P25. Yin et al. reported that C1 inhibited Rhizoctonia solani AG8 radial growth in dual culture and significantly reduced wheat root rot while increasing wheat fresh root weight under AG8 challenge.

name: Wheat Synthetic Consortium C6
description: A four-member mixed-genus wheat-rhizosphere synthetic consortium (SynCom 6/C6) composed of Streptomyces sp. B6, Chryseobacterium sp. B7, Pseudomonas sp. B12, and Sphingomonas sp. B17. Yin et al. reported that C6 inhibited Rhizoctonia solani AG8 radial growth in dual culture and produced auxin in vitro as a whole consortium.

name: Wine Yeast Five-Species Strain-Substitution Consortium
description: A defined five-species wine yeast consortium assembled from Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Lachancea thermotolerans, Hanseniaspora uvarum, Starmerella bacillaris, and Torulaspora delbrueckii. Wang et al. 2026 represented each species with two phenotypically diverging strains and systematically perturbed the consortium by species drop-out and strain substitution to quantify fermentation kinetics, sugar utilization, population dynamics, primary metabolites, and major volatile compounds. Species drop-out and strain substitution both shifted population, growth, and metabolic outputs, with non-Saccharomyces substitutions affecting metabolic output more broadly than S. cerevisiae strain choice.

name: Wine Yeast Three-Species Contact Consortium
description: A defined three-member wine yeast consortium built from fluorescently labeled Saccharomyces cerevisiae VIN13, Lachancea thermotolerans IWBT Y1240, and Torulaspora delbrueckii LO544 to compare direct cell-cell contact against metabolic-only contact in a multi-membrane bioreactor. Asmus et al. 2026 cultured the yeasts in yeast nitrogen base with glucose and ammonium sulfate, either together in the same 700 mL vessel or separated by 0.1 um membranes with continuous medium exchange, and measured 12 h growth, extracellular glucose, ammonia and amino acids, and S. cerevisiae RNA-seq at 5 and 9 h.

name: Wolffia Mankai Endosphere Cobamide Guild
description: A host-filtered bacterial endosphere community from the edible aquatic plant Wolffia globosa Mankai, sampled from industrial rotating raceway cultivation. Amplicon and shotgun metagenomic analyses showed that Mankai medium, phyllosphere, and surface-sterilized internal-tissue fractions formed distinct communities; downstream MAG analysis of the endosphere found a low-diversity Proteobacteria/Pseudomonadota-dominated consortium in which Alphaproteobacterial members encoded near-complete cobamide biosynthesis pathways, while many Gammaproteobacteria and Bacteroidota lineages carried incomplete pathways enriched for cobamide salvage and remodeling. A MAG-derived functional-complementarity network placed Hyphomicrobium zavarzinii, Methylobacterium, Devosia, Labrys, and Ferrovibrionaceae among the inferred producer-side taxa, supporting a producer-salvager model for cobamide metabolism in the plant-associated niche.

name: Wollastonite Ramichloridium-Talaromyces Fungal Consortium
description: A defined two-fungus mixed culture of Ramichloridium apiculatum CMS-1 and Talaromyces pseudofuniculosus hzt-3′ grown with wollastonite in modified Czapek liquid medium. The source study varied the CMS-1:hzt-3′ inoculation ratio and found that 20% CMS-1 plus 80% hzt-3′ gave the strongest Ca2+ and Si4+ leaching, with CMS-1-derived extracellular polysaccharides and proteins cross-feeding hzt-3′ organic-acid and amino-acid production.

name: Yarrowia lipolytica Division-of-Labor Lipid Consortium
description: A defined two-strain Yarrowia lipolytica consortium engineered to convert lignocellulose-derived oligosaccharides into lipids through metabolic division of labor. The system partitions hydrolysis and assimilation between a cellobiose-specialized YBGL3/YBGL1 lineage and a xylooligosaccharide-specialized YBXT-XR lineage, then benchmarks the consortium against a single multifunctional YBXT-XR-BGL3 strain. In mixed glucose, cellobiose, and xylooligosaccharide coculture, the division-of-labor consortium raised lipid accumulation above the monoculture benchmark and shifted toward the YBXT-XR partner after cellobiose depletion.

name: Yogurt Two-Species Starter Culture
description: A defined thermophilic dairy fermentation community composed of Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus. The two lactic-acid bacteria form the canonical yogurt starter association, where metabolite exchange accelerates milk acidification: S. thermophilus provides formate, carbon dioxide, and urease-dependent ammonia/carbon dioxide effects that stimulate the lactobacillus, while proteolytic activity of L. delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus releases peptides and amino acids that support the more weakly proteolytic streptococcus.

name: Zymomonas-E. coli Exometabolomics-Designed Obligate Mutualism
description: A defined synthetic obligate mutualism pairing auxotrophic Zymomonas mobilis with auxotrophic Escherichia coli. Exometabolomics of Z. mobilis spent medium identified amino acid exometabolites used to select E. coli proA, pheA, and ilvA auxotroph partners, while mutant fitness profiling selected a Z. mobilis ZMO0748 auxotroph whose rescue was linked to glutathione-related metabolites in E. coli spent medium. The system is DOE-relevant because it was developed by LBNL and Sandia researchers with DOE BER support as a synthetic microbial ecology platform for more resilient biotechnology processes.
